rules.statement: The offspring of a Kandyan father by a Low-country Sinhalese woman cannot be said to be Kandyan and must be governed by the general law of the land.
rules.supporting_quote: As regards nationality, the District Judge is apparently using the word in its strictly legal sense. It is only when the word is used in that sense that it can be said that the wife takes the husband's nationality and the child the father's. Thus, every subject of the Crown, be he Sinhalese, Tamil, Chinese, or Hottentot, is British in nationality, that is to say, he is subject to the British flag; but where the word is used in a looser and more popular sense-in the sense of race for instance-the rule relied on by the District Judge has no application at all.
